answer: A new identity enters after one season at the forge, where a master smith watches it shape timber into a beam and stamps the work with a velvet seal. The seal is logged in a ledger, and if the same hands present a second identity, the seal is struck and the master loses its wage. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 seasons of labor at $2,500 a season, $2,500,000 in wages, while one honest agent pays nothing and enters on a season of real work.
